Title: SINAN - Yellow fever notifications
What it contains: Individual notification records of suspected and confirmed human yellow fever, including notification and symptom-onset dates, municipality of residence and of probable infection, case classification and outcome.
Key variables: Notification date; symptom onset date; municipality of residence (IBGE 6-digit); municipality of probable infection; final classification; evolution/death; vaccination status
Who holds it: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS (national); state and municipal surveillance secretariats feed the system
Producer: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)
Contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
Native spatial resolution: Individual record, geocoded to municipality of residence and of probable infection
Temporal resolution: Daily (event dates), aggregated to epidemiological week
Update frequency: Continuous notification; public files consolidated annually, preliminary files updated more often
Latency: Weeks to months for preliminary data; ~1 year for closed annual files
Licence: Open government data (Lei de Acesso à Informação); attribution to MS/SVSA expected
Sharing conditions: Public de-identified files may be redistributed. Identified line-lists require a data-use agreement with the surveillance authority and ethics approval.
Personal data: Public files de-identified; municipality of residence retained
Linkage key: IBGE municipality code (6-digit in health files; divide 7-digit code by 10 to match)
Known limitations: Under-notification in low-access areas; municipality of probable infection is often missing or inferred; retrospective reclassification changes historical counts.

Title: SINAN - Dengue notifications
What it contains: Individual notification records of suspected and confirmed dengue, with symptom-onset date, municipality of residence, laboratory results, serotype where typed, severity classification and outcome.
Key variables: Symptom onset date; notification date; municipality and district of residence; serotype; laboratory confirmation; severity; hospitalisation; evolution
Who holds it: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS; municipal data flow through COVISA in São Paulo
Producer: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)
Contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
Spatial coverage: Brazil (analysis subset: municipality of São Paulo)
Native spatial resolution: Individual record; public files resolve to municipality only
Analysis unit: Municipality (public files); census sector (restricted COVISA extract, see HEA-003)
Temporal resolution: Daily event dates, aggregated to epidemiological week
Update frequency: Continuous notification; annual consolidated files, weekly preliminary panels
Latency: 1-4 weeks for preliminary counts; ~1 year for closed files
Licence: Open government data; attribution to MS/SVSA expected
Sharing conditions: Public files redistributable. Sub-municipal geography is not in the public release and must be requested from COVISA.
Known limitations: Public geography stops at the municipality, which is too coarse for a heat-island analysis; serotype typed for a small subset of cases.

Title: COVISA arbovirus surveillance line-list, São Paulo
Title (PT): Vigilância de arboviroses - COVISA, Município de São Paulo
What it contains: Municipal arbovirus surveillance records for São Paulo with residential address geocoding, allowing cases to be assigned to census sectors, districts and weather-station catchments. Includes the subset of cases with a laboratory-confirmed serotype.
Key variables: Geocoded residence (point or census sector); symptom onset date; case classification; serotype for laboratory-typed cases; age; sex
Who holds it: COVISA - Coordenadoria de Vigilância em Saúde, Secretaria Municipal da Saúde de São Paulo
Contact: To be confirmed - COVISA arbovirus surveillance division
Native spatial resolution: Address point, aggregated to census sector or district for release
Update frequency: Weekly internally; release schedule to be agreed
Formats: CSV or database extract, to be agreed
Licence: Not applicable - governed by the data-use agreement
Sharing conditions: Requires CEP/CONEP ethics approval, then a formal data-sharing agreement with COVISA. Aggregated outputs only; no address-level redistribution; publication drafts shared with COVISA before submission.
Personal data: Yes - geocoded residence is potentially identifying. Aggregate to census sector before analysis and suppress small counts.
Linkage key: IBGE census sector code (2022); epidemiological week
Known limitations: Geocoding completeness varies by year and by neighbourhood; small-area counts require suppression rules.
Holding status: To be acquired - awaiting ethics approval, then confirmation with COVISA
Record status: Draft - confirm with COVISA once ethics approval is granted

Title: SINAN - American cutaneous leishmaniasis notifications
What it contains: Individual notification records of American cutaneous leishmaniasis, with clinical form, municipality of residence and of probable infection, diagnostic criteria, treatment and outcome.
Key variables: Notification and onset dates; municipality of residence and probable infection; clinical form (cutaneous/mucosal); diagnostic criterion; treatment; evolution; occupation
Who holds it: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS; Secretaria de Estado da Saúde do Pará
Producer: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)
Contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
Native spatial resolution: Individual record, municipality of residence and of probable infection
Temporal resolution: Daily event dates, aggregated to month
Licence: Open government data; attribution to MS/SVSA expected
Sharing conditions: Public de-identified files may be redistributed with attribution.
Known limitations: Place of infection frequently differs from place of residence in a mobile rural population; under-diagnosis in areas with limited health-service access.

Title: SI-PNI immunisation coverage
What it contains: Doses administered and coverage estimates by municipality, age group and immunobiological, including yellow fever and dengue vaccines. Used as a confounder and as denominator context.
Key variables: Doses applied; immunobiological; dose number; age group; municipality; administration date
Who holds it: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS - Programa Nacional de Imunizações
Producer: Sistema de Informação do Programa Nacional de Imunizações (SI-PNI)
Contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
Native spatial resolution: Municipality (aggregate); individual dose records in the nominal system
Licence: Open government data
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Known limitations: Coverage denominators rely on population projections that drifted from the 2022 census; campaign doses can be recorded late.

Title: Non-human primate epizootic records
Title (PT): Vigilância de epizootias em primatas não humanos
What it contains: Reports of sickness or death in non-human primates investigated for yellow fever, the earliest available signal of sylvatic virus circulation and therefore a candidate outcome ahead of human cases.
Key variables: Event date; municipality; species; laboratory result; classification
Who holds it: Ministério da Saúde / SVSA; state surveillance; SISS-Geo (Fiocruz) for citizen reports
Update frequency: Continuous, with reporting peaks during outbreaks
Licence: To be confirmed
Sharing conditions: To be confirmed with SVSA and Fiocruz.
Known limitations: Strongly effort-dependent - reporting rises where surveillance teams are active and during known outbreaks, so absence is not evidence of absence.

Title: ERA5-Land reanalysis - daily surface variables
Title (PT): Reanálise ERA5-Land - variáveis diárias de superfície
What it contains: Global land-surface climate reconstruction. The laboratory downloads minimum, mean and maximum 2 m air temperature, total precipitation, 2 m dew-point temperature, 10 m wind components and surface pressure, then reduces each to one value per municipality.
Key variables: Tmin, Tmean, Tmax (2 m); total precipitation; dew-point temperature; 10 m U and V wind; surface pressure
Who holds it: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, through the Copernicus Climate Data Store
Contact: Copernicus Climate Data Store, registered account and API key
Temporal resolution: Hourly native; downloaded daily, aggregated to epidemiological week (YF, dengue) or month (ACL)
Update frequency: Rolling, about 2-3 months behind real time
Licence: Copernicus licence - free reuse with attribution
Sharing conditions: Raw data freely redistributable under the Copernicus licence. Derived municipality series may be published with attribution.
Known limitations: Temperatures arrive in Kelvin (subtract 273.15). A reanalysis is a model product, not a measurement, and 9 km cannot resolve within-city heat contrasts - use CLI-004 for that. Coastal and steep-terrain municipalities are least reliable. The Pará download was extended to dew-point temperature in August 2026; series before that date do not contain it.

Title: ERA5-Land weekly climatological normals
Title (PT): Normais climatológicas semanais derivadas do ERA5-Land
What it contains: Pre-computed long-term weekly averages per municipality, used as the reference against which any week of any year is called normal or anomalous.
Key variables: Weekly normals for Tmin (1981-2010 and 1991-2020), Tmax, precipitation, relative humidity and wind speed (1981-2010)
Who holds it: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory (derived); ERA5-Land upstream
Update frequency: Recomputed when the baseline period changes (roughly every decade)
Access URL: Internal repository; see DER-001 for the published equivalents
Licence: To be assigned - CC BY 4.0 proposed
Sharing conditions: Shareable with partners on request; publish alongside the paper.
Linkage key: IBGE municipality code; ISO week number
Known limitations: The choice of baseline changes the answer. The 1991-2020 normal is warmer and flags anomalies more conservatively than 1981-2010; state which baseline is used in every output.

Title: Large-scale climate indices - ENSO, IOD, PDO
What it contains: Single global time series describing El Niño-Southern Oscillation, the Indian Ocean Dipole and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, used as background drivers common to all municipalities.
Key variables: ENSO index; IOD index; PDO index
Who holds it: Obtained through the InfoDengue Sprint 2024-25 dataset; original indices from NOAA and equivalent agencies
Producer: NOAA and partner agencies, redistributed by InfoDengue
Analysis unit: One value per week, applied nationally
Update frequency: Weekly to monthly depending on index
Access URL: InfoDengue Sprint dataset; NOAA for originals
Licence: Open, attribution to originating agency
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Known limitations: No spatial contrast, so these can only explain shared year-to-year variation, not why one municipality differs from its neighbour.

Title: CGE/CGESP municipal weather-station network, São Paulo
Title (PT): Rede de estações meteorológicas do CGE - Município de São Paulo
What it contains: The municipal network of automatic weather and rainfall stations operated by São Paulo's climate emergency management centre. This is the only source fine enough to separate hot from cool neighbourhoods inside the city, which is what the heat-island analysis needs.
Key variables: Air temperature; relative humidity; rainfall; wind; station coordinates and installation history
Who holds it: CGE - Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências Climáticas, Prefeitura de São Paulo
Contact: To be confirmed - CGE technical division
Native spatial resolution: Point stations; station density and catchment size to be documented
Analysis unit: Station catchment or interpolated surface, joined to census sectors
Temporal resolution: Sub-hourly to hourly, aggregated to daily and weekly
Update frequency: Continuous, near real time on the public portal
Latency: Minutes for the live portal; archive access to be confirmed
Formats: To be confirmed - web portal, possible CSV export
Licence: To be confirmed
Sharing conditions: To be agreed with CGE at project start, together with archive access, the station history file and the citation terms. Expect attribution and possibly an acknowledgement or co-authorship arrangement for the historical archive.
Known limitations: Stations are unevenly distributed and periphery coverage is thinner than the centre, which risks under-measuring the hottest and most dengue-affected areas. Record gaps and instrument changes need a station-history file.
Holding status: To be acquired - terms agreed at project start
Record status: Draft - confirm with CGE at project start

Title: INMET automatic station network
Title (PT): Rede de estações automáticas do INMET
What it contains: The national network of automatic surface stations. Its role here is validation: it is the ground measurement used to quantify the bias in the ERA5-Land reanalysis (CLI-001), municipality by municipality, with particular attention to Pará where stations are sparse.
Key variables: Air temperature (instantaneous, max, min); relative humidity; precipitation; wind; pressure; radiation
Who holds it: INMET - Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia
Spatial coverage: Brazil - station network, sparse in the Amazon
Analysis unit: Station, matched to the containing municipality
Licence: Open government data, attribution to INMET
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Linkage key: Station code and coordinates; IBGE municipality code; date
Known limitations: Very sparse in Pará, so the bias estimate will have wide uncertainty over much of the ACL study area, and that uncertainty should be reported rather than smoothed over. Gaps and sensor changes are common and are not always flagged in the files.
Holding status: To be acquired - bias quantification against ERA5-Land

Title: ANA hydrological station network (HidroWeb)
What it contains: River stage and discharge measured at gauging stations on Amazonian rivers. This is the measured alternative to using extreme rainfall as a stand-in for flooding: a river level above its flood reference is an observation, not an inference.
Key variables: River stage (cm); discharge (m3/s); rainfall at co-located gauges; flood reference level
Who holds it: ANA - Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico
Producer: ANA, with state and utility operators
Contact: HidroWeb portal and the ANA API
Spatial coverage: Brazil - station network; denser on main Amazonian channels than on tributaries
Analysis unit: Station, assigned to downstream municipalities in its catchment
Temporal coverage: Varies by station; many Amazonian records run from the 1970s
Temporal resolution: Daily stage readings; sub-daily at telemetric stations
Update frequency: Daily to near real time at telemetric stations
Latency: Hours at telemetric stations; months for validated historical series
Licence: Open government data, attribution to ANA
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Linkage key: Station code with coordinates; IBGE municipality code of the catchment; date
Known limitations: A gauge measures the river, not the floodplain. Stations sit on main channels, so flooding in small tributary settlements - where ACL transmission concentrates - may not register. Assess coverage against the case municipalities before committing.
Holding status: Candidate - under assessment for the inundation layer

Title: MODIS vegetation greenness (NDVI)
What it contains: Satellite measure of how green and dense vegetation is. Two variants are held: a ~1 km series obtained through NASA AppEEARS for the yellow fever work, and the 250 m MOD13Q1 product obtained through Google Earth Engine for the leishmaniasis work.
Key variables: NDVI (maximum, mean, minimum, standard deviation per municipality)
Who holds it: NASA - LP DAAC, accessed through AppEEARS and Google Earth Engine
Spatial coverage: Global; downloaded for Brazil (YF) and Pará (ACL)
Licence: NASA open data, attribution requested
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Known limitations: Persistent cloud in the Amazon thins the usable composites. Monthly NDVI is joined onto a weekly panel in the YF work, so the greenness value repeats across weeks within a month.

Title: MapBiomas land cover and land use
Title (PT): MapBiomas - cobertura e uso da terra
What it contains: Annual national land-cover map from Landsat imagery. Supplies forest cover and fragmentation for the yellow fever work, and areas of deforestation, secondary regrowth, agriculture and water for the leishmaniasis work.
Key variables: Class areas per municipality-year: forest, secondary vegetation, agriculture, pasture, urban, water; derived fragmentation metrics
Who holds it: MapBiomas project (Brazilian civil-society and academic network)
Native spatial resolution: 30 m (Landsat); municipality statistics also distributed pre-summarised
Analysis unit: Municipality x year (percentage or hectares per class)
Update frequency: Annual, with a new collection roughly every year
Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
Sharing conditions: Redistributable under CC BY-SA with attribution to MapBiomas and the collection number.
Known limitations: Collections are reprocessed retrospectively, so a series downloaded today will not match one downloaded two years ago. Always record the collection number.

Title: Built-up surface index (NDBI)
What it contains: Satellite measure of how built-up or bare a surface is, derived from Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery in Google Earth Engine and reduced to a yearly median per municipality.
Key variables: NDBI (yearly median per municipality)
Who holds it: USGS (Landsat) and ESA (Sentinel-2), accessed through Google Earth Engine
Producer: IPSP, computed in Google Earth Engine
Licence: Landsat public domain; Sentinel-2 Copernicus licence
Sharing conditions: Derived series redistributable with attribution to USGS and ESA.
Known limitations: The sensor changes in 2017, so the 30 m and 10 m halves of the series are not directly comparable. Treat the break explicitly in any trend model.

Title: Land surface temperature for urban heat islands
Title (PT): Temperatura de superfície (LST) para ilhas de calor
What it contains: Thermal satellite imagery giving surface temperature across the city, used to map the heat-island pattern between the sparse weather stations and to characterise every census sector.
Key variables: Land surface temperature; derived surface urban heat island intensity per census sector
Who holds it: USGS (Landsat 8/9) and NASA (MODIS), accessed through Google Earth Engine
Native spatial resolution: 100 m thermal resampled to 30 m (Landsat); 1 km (MODIS)
Temporal resolution: 16-day revisit per satellite (about 8 days combined); MODIS twice daily
Licence: Landsat public domain; NASA open data
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Known limitations: Surface temperature is not air temperature, and cloud cover removes many São Paulo summer scenes - exactly the season the dengue analysis cares about. Use as a spatial pattern to complement CLI-004, not as a substitute for it.

Title: Terrain elevation and slope (SRTM)
What it contains: Digital elevation model used to derive mean slope and relief range per municipality, as context for temperature and for vector habitat.
Key variables: Elevation; mean slope; relief range per municipality
Who holds it: NASA, accessed through AppEEARS
Licence: NASA open data
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Known limitations: A single 2000 survey; no change over time. A municipality mean hides the range that matters in mountainous terrain.

Title: WorldClim elevation (coarse backup)
What it contains: Coarse global elevation layer held as a fallback. Retained in the catalogue for completeness and explicitly not used in the models.
Key variables: Elevation
Who holds it: WorldClim (University of California, Davis)
Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Known limitations: Too coarse for municipality-level work - superseded by ENV-005 and not used in any model.

Title: Human footprint index, HIBR-10
What it contains: Human Impact on the Brazilian Environment at 10 m resolution (HIBR-10): a national raster scoring human pressure on every 10 m cell from land cover, building density, and distance to major roads, railways and navigable waterways. It is the highest-resolution human footprint layer available for Brazil.
Key variables: Weighted human footprint score, 0-100 (rescaled from 0-10); component layers supplied separately
Who holds it: Zenodo deposit 10.5281/zenodo.15306587 (Hamilton & Presotto, 2025)
Producer: Presotto A, Hamilton S, Izar P. A 10-meter resolution human footprint dataset to support biodiversity and conservation studies in Brazil. Scientific Data 2025;12:1754. doi:10.1038/s41597-025-06034-0
Contact: Stuart Hamilton, East Carolina University (corresponding author)
Spatial coverage: Brazil, all biomes; clipped to State of Pará for this project
Native spatial resolution: 10 m (86.5 billion cells), projected EPSG:5880 SIRGAS 2000 / Brazil Polyconic
Analysis unit: Municipality (zonal mean of the footprint score)
Temporal coverage: Static - built from 2023 Sentinel-2 land cover and post-2020 building footprints
Update frequency: By release version; the file is HFI_Weighted_vx.tif, higher x is a later release
Licence: Article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Check the Zenodo deposit terms before redistributing any derived layer, since NC-ND would restrict it.
Sharing conditions: Cite Presotto et al. 2025 and the Zenodo DOI. Confirm the deposit licence before publishing a derived or reweighted layer.
Known limitations: NoData is coded 255, not null - set it explicitly or the zonal means are wrong. Scores are rescaled 0-100 from the published 0-10 scale. The aggregation weights (40% land cover, 40% building density, 10% major roads, 5% railways, 5% waterways) are the authors' choices for primate conservation; the authors intend users to reweight for their own question, which for ACL might mean raising forest-edge and waterway terms. A single snapshot, so no change over the 2000-2024 study period.

Title: Satellite surface-water and flood extent
Title (PT): Extensão de água superficial e inundação por satélite
What it contains: Mapped water surface through time, from the JRC Global Surface Water record and MapBiomas Água. Together these give seasonal and permanent water extent per municipality, which is the closest thing to a real inundation layer without new field data.
Key variables: Water occurrence and seasonality; monthly water extent; flooded area per municipality-month
Who holds it: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC); MapBiomas project
Producer: JRC Global Surface Water (Landsat); MapBiomas Água
Contact: Google Earth Engine account; MapBiomas platform
Spatial coverage: Global (JRC) and Brazil (MapBiomas Água); subset State of Pará
Analysis unit: Municipality x month (flooded area and share of municipal area)
Licence: JRC open data (CC BY 4.0); MapBiomas CC BY-SA 4.0
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution to each product.
Known limitations: Optical sensors cannot see water under forest canopy or through Amazonian cloud, which is exactly when and where flooding matters. Treat as a lower bound. If canopy flooding proves important, radar (Sentinel-1) would be the next step, at a higher processing cost.
Holding status: Candidate - under assessment for the inundation layer

Title: IBGE municipal boundaries
What it contains: The official municipal boundary geometry. Every gridded climate and environmental layer is reduced to municipality values against this mesh, so it is the join that holds the whole catalogue together.
Key variables: Municipality polygon; 7-digit IBGE code; name; state; area
Who holds it: IBGE - Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística
Licence: Open government data, attribution to IBGE
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
Linkage key: IBGE municipality code - 7-digit here, 6-digit in health files (cod6 = cod7 // 10)
Known limitations: Municipalities are created and boundaries change between editions, so long time series need a fixed reference year stated up front.

Title: IBGE 2022 census - sector-level indicators
What it contains: Population, income, household density and sanitation indicators at census-sector level, the finest official social geography available. Supplies both the denominator and the main confounders for the São Paulo heat-island analysis.
Key variables: Resident population; household density; income; water supply; sewerage connection; waste collection; sector polygon
Who holds it: IBGE
Spatial coverage: Brazil; subset municipality of São Paulo
Update frequency: Every 10 years, with staged releases of each indicator set
Licence: Open government data, attribution to IBGE
Sharing conditions: Redistributable with attribution. Small-count suppression rules already applied by IBGE.
Known limitations: Sector boundaries changed between 2010 and 2022, so pre-2022 dengue years cannot be joined to 2022 sectors without an areal-interpolation step. A single snapshot cannot capture change across the 2015-2024 study window.

Title: Static municipal environmental context
What it contains: A fixed table of Köppen climate class, biome and altitude per municipality, used as unchanging context in the models.
Key variables: Köppen class; biome; altitude
Who holds it: InfoDengue Sprint 2024-25 environmental table
Licence: To be confirmed
Sharing conditions: Confirm the InfoDengue redistribution terms before republishing.
Known limitations: One class per municipality flattens real internal variation in large municipalities.

Title: Municipality zonal statistics and climate anomaly indicators
Title (PT): Estatísticas zonais e indicadores de anomalia climática
What it contains: The published municipality-level climate summaries and anomaly indicators produced by the laboratory, deposited on Zenodo so that others can reuse the processing rather than repeat it.
Key variables: Municipality zonal statistics for the ERA5-Land variables; anomaly indicators against the weekly normals
Who holds it: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory; hosted by Zenodo
Native spatial resolution: Derived from the ~9 km ERA5-Land grid
Licence: As stated on the Zenodo record
Sharing conditions: Openly citable by DOI. Cite the deposit version used.
Known limitations: Fixed at the deposit date; re-run against current ERA5-Land for recent years.

Title: Yellow fever exposure indicators
What it contains: Exposure variables built from minimum temperature rather than downloaded: warm-night counts, warm spells and anomalies against the weekly normals. These are the actual model inputs.
Key variables: Days with Tmin above 17 C; runs of 7 or more consecutive warm days in April-September; Tmin anomaly against the 1981-2010 and 1991-2020 normals; extreme-rainfall weeks above the 99th percentile
Who holds it: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory
Access: Internal - to be published with the paper
Licence: CC BY 4.0 proposed on publication
Sharing conditions: Shareable with collaborators now; deposit publicly at acceptance.
Known limitations: Thresholds (17 C, 7 days, 99th percentile) are analytical choices, not properties of the data - record the version used with every result. Flooding has no dataset and is approximated by extreme rainfall.

Title: Leishmaniasis climate and vector indicators
What it contains: Indicators built from temperature, rainfall and humidity for the ACL models, including a simple sand-fly population simulation. Relative humidity is computed from ERA5-Land dew-point using the same method as the yellow fever work.
Key variables: Relative humidity derived from 2 m dew-point and air temperature; seasonal temperature, rainfall and humidity anomalies (2000-2024 baseline); accumulated warmth above 10 C; favourable-infection flag (22-28 C and rainfall above 50 mm); simulated sand-fly density; 1-8 month lags; 3-month rolling mean of case counts
Who holds it: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory
Access: Internal - to be published with the paper
Licence: CC BY 4.0 proposed on publication
Sharing conditions: Shareable with collaborators now; deposit publicly at acceptance.
Known limitations: The favourable-infection thresholds and the vector model are assumptions carried into every downstream result; document and sensitivity-test them. The 2000-2024 anomaly baseline is the study period itself, which shrinks apparent trends. Humidity is derived, not measured - validate against INMET stations (CLI-005).
